s: INFO.MEASURES() returns one row per measure with [Name], [Expression], [Description], [TableID] and more.
Join to INFO.TABLES() for table names, filter blank descriptions.
Keep the query in the repo; run it before releases.
Read the CSV into a dictionary; loop over Model.AllMeasures.
Dry run: print matches, overwrites (existing non-empty description that differs) and measures missing from the dictionary; change nothing.
Apply: set Description where empty, and overwrite only when a flag allows it.
Run it in Tabular Editor against the PBIP's model folder, save, commit, open a PR: the TMDL diff shows exactly what changed.

code.title: Tabular Editor script: descriptions from the KPI dictionary
src: var dryRun = true; var allowOverwrite = false;
var dict = lines.Select(l => l.Split(new[]{','}, 2)).ToDictionary(p => p[0].Trim('"'), p => p[1].Trim('"'));
if (!dict.ContainsKey(m.Name)) { report.AppendLine("NOT IN DICTIONARY: " + m.DaxObjectFullName); continue; }

api-xmla-1.check: Dry run lists matches, overwrites and unknown measures; apply mode changes only what the flags allow; the PR diff shows description lines only.

s: List partitions: EVALUATE INFO.PARTITIONS() or in SSMS/Tabular Editor; incremental refresh names them by period (e.g. 2026Q1, or months for the latest period).
Send a TMSL refresh for that partition through the XMLA endpoint (SSMS → New XMLA query) or enhanced refresh via REST with objects=[{table, partition}].
Compare duration with a full refresh; check the partition's RefreshedTime changed and others didn't.
api-xmla-2.check: Only the targeted partition's refresh time changes; duration is a fraction of a full refresh.
api-xmla-2.note: Partition names depend on the incremental refresh policy (yearly, quarterly, monthly, daily granularity for the most recent periods). Read them first; don't guess.
